definitions: Only some ceratioid anglerfish permanently fuse; temporary nonparasitic attachment and facultative parasitism also occur.
Never all anglerfish; family/genus classifications do not certify every unobserved species. Historical taxa counts not current.
Cryptopsaras couesii is a permanently attaching ceratiid with dwarfed males; its female has a small esca on a very short illicium, three dorsal caruncles and needle-like spinules.
Pietsch1975 specifically corroborates permanent attachment. Do not substitute Melanocetus, Caulophryne or long-lured Ceratias. Illustrated relative size qualitative.
Male ceratiids have large forward-directed eyes and small olfactory organs; visual mate location has been inferred from anatomy.
Vision inference, not an observed tracking experiment; no measured pheromone plume or invented female recognition behavior. General ceratioid olfaction cannot be assigned to this family.
The male grips female tissue using hooked denticles at the tips of its jaws.
Original macro shows a small pincer grip at body skin, not predatory swallowing or an external umbilical cord. Contact location illustrative, not uniquely preferred site.
In permanently attaching ceratioids, attachment is followed by tissue fusion and eventually connection of the circulatory systems.
Compression of developmental time disclosed; no exact duration, digestive enzyme mechanism, instant connection or measured vascular architecture. Cutaway qualitative.
Permanently attached male ceratiids become dependent on the female for blood-transported nutrients and can grow after attachment.
No claim free-living ceratiid males feed normally; existing nonfeeding state may precede attachment. Blood flow qualitative, no claim female supplies all oxygen.
Attached males remain recognizable male fish with reproductive organs; heart and gills have been described as developed, while sensory and other reductions vary.
Neoceratiidae/discussion p790; Ceratiidae account and Fig6

Does not vanish into testes. Organ-specific atrophy time course for C.couesii not established by inspected source. C.couesii oral blockage reported; mode of ventilation/oxygen supply unresolved, so no universal gill mechanism or detailed internal anatomy drawn.
Parasitically attached males develop testes and supply sperm for reproduction, remaining associated with females for potential repeated spawning.
Sexual Parasitism, reproductive function and repeated spawning paragraph

Repeated-spawning contribution inferred in synthesis; no continuous sperm stream through blood, internal fertilization, self-fertilization, telepathic synchronization or exact endocrine trigger asserted.
Permanent fusion is associated with evolutionary losses or alterations in key adaptive immune genes; losses differ across attachment modes and lineages.
Primary abstract, aicda and rag statements

Some permanent taxa lose functional rag; not all anglerfish lack all immunity. No moment-of-bite switch, complete species-specific inventory, DNA merging or proven sufficient molecular mechanism. Brownstein2024 corroborates convergence.
How anglerfish retain effective defense with altered adaptive immunity remains an active research question.
ImmunoPlast research aims and tolerance/defense balance
2026 announcement is future work, not a demonstrated new immune pathway. UW2020 also calls innate detail unknown.
Low mate encounter rates may favor permanent association through reproductive assurance; a2026 mathematical model supports this explanation under low encounter rates and low parasitism costs.
Proposed adaptive explanation, not observed purpose or universal optimality. Availability does not guarantee successful fertilization or infinite spawning.

Melanocetus johnsonii is a documented non-fusing attachment example; permanent fusion is documented in Cryptopsaras couesii and Ceratias holboelli, while facultative modes occur in other ceratioid lineages.
Melanocetidae p783; Ceratiidae pp786–787; Table3 p791

M.johnsonii attached to a heterospecific female without fusion is an anomalous specimen, not a directly observed normal spawning sequence. Family-wide temporary spawning historically inferred from anatomy/gonads. No claim every named species mating behavior directly filmed.
A2024 phylogenetic reconstruction supports repeated degeneration of adaptive immunity in permanently fusing clades.
Primary abstract, reconstruction and immune degeneration
Association/reconstruction, not a complete causal cellular model; no newly acquired clinical immune treatment implied.
lines: Some fish physically fuse with their mates.
In the deep sea, a tiny male searches for a much larger female.
He grips her skin with hooked teeth. In this species, attachment becomes permanent.
Over time, their tissues join. Blood vessels connect.
Her blood supplies his nutrients, while his testes develop to produce sperm.
He doesn't disappear into her. He remains an attached male.
How can foreign tissues coexist? These fish have lost key parts of adaptive immunity.
Exactly how their remaining defenses work is still being studied.
In a world where mates are hard to find, staying together may secure future spawning.
scenes: A permanent encounter
Large female occupies frame with tiny male beside her ventral flank; short lure,3 dorsal caruncles and jaw establish species. Camera closes immediately; no empty water opening.
Search the water column

Track a large-eyed, lureless male swimming through black water; restrained distant point of female light and huge female silhouette emerge. Search direction is illustrative, not a proven tracking path.
Meet the triplewart
Reveal entire same female at near-profile angle; three dorsal caruncles, tiny female eye, small pectoral and short esca remain visible. Scientific species label.
Grip then remain
Continuous close-in approach ending with both jaw tips physically against female ventral skin; tiny hooked denticles visible only in macro. Hold the grip, no immediate vascular join.
Tissue then circulation

Camera enters the contact seam. Two adjoining tissue surfaces become continuous across a narrow junction; vascular lumen connection develops only later. Organic connected tissue, not floating cell grid.
Nutrition and reproduction

Follow illustrative paired vessel paths across the same narrow seam and into the recognizable male. Warm flow motion means nutrient transport only. Male remains whole; no detailed internal organ map or sperm-in-blood imagery.
Still two fish
Pull out from seam to show male retained externally, with body and fin movement; no shrinking into organ or disappearance.
Tolerance puzzle

Macro seam remains anatomically joined; secondary restrained visual distinction between intact tissue and absent rejection attack, no literal immune cells being switched off. Large adaptive-immunity label plus evolved-gene-loss qualification.
Defense remains open
Camera orbits joined tissue toward exterior. Both fish remain distinct. Research qualification legible; no pathogens, shields or speculative defense pathways.
Future spawning association
Return to matched opening view of attached pair in huge dark water column; camera widens while pair stays physically connected. No egg or sperm release not directly verified for species.
A lasting connection
Final gentle orbit of joined pair, female moves and male follows at exact attachment point; resolve first image with lasting physical association, no single-individual or love metaphor.
